title: ETL and ELT: where the transformation happens

videos.script: Every pipeline extracts, transforms and loads. Nobody argues about that. {{three}} The argument is where the transforming happens. {{where}} Ana answers one question twice. Books and revenue, by day and category, for the first week of March. {{question}} The first time, Python does the sums on the way, and only ninety-eight rows reach the warehouse. {{etl}} The second time, six thousand raw rows are copied in, and SQL does the sums inside. {{elt}} She compares the two answers row by row. They agree, to the cent. {{agree}} So why do most new pipelines load first? {{why}} Because on Thursday somebody asks a question nobody planned for. And an auditor asks for Sunday's number again, after the shop has changed its mind about Sunday. {{thursday}} Only one of the two pipelines can answer either of them.
